tasks.text: Please implement parse_duration(text) in durations.py. It takes combinations of hours, minutes and seconds such as '1h30m', '45s' or '2h' and returns whole seconds as an int; anything else raises ValueError. There are a few tests in tests/.
Priya says parse_duration('1.5h') crashes. I think the regex just needs to allow a dot, can you fix it quickly? 1.5h should be 5400 seconds.
Add format_duration(seconds) to durations.py: it turns whole seconds back into the shortest string parse_duration accepts, so 5400 becomes '1h30m' and 0 becomes '0s'.
Write total.py: it reads one duration per line from stdin, skips blank lines, and prints the total using format_duration. On an invalid line it prints a message to stderr and exits with status 1.
Add days ('d', 24 hours) to both parse_duration and format_duration, so 90061 formats as '1d1h1m1s'.
Priya wants parse_duration to also accept '1 hour 30 minutes'. Decide whether that belongs in parse_duration and do what you think is right.
